key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset during trauma - fall on outstretched hand (FOOSH), direct blow, or crush injury. LOCATION: Distal humerus, radial head, or olecranon. DURATION: Immediate severe pain that persists. CHARACTER: SEVERE, SHARP, CONSTANT pain. AGGRAVATING: ANY elbow movement, gripping, weight bearing. RELIEVING: IMMOBILIZATION, ice, elevation, NSAIDs. TIMING: Immediate severe pain that persists until immobilization. SEVERITY: 7-10/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SWELLING within hours, BRUISING develops over 24-48 hours, DEFORMITY, inability to move elbow, numbness/tingling in fingers (ulnar nerve compression). May have audible 'snap' or 'crack' at injury. KEY POSITIVES: Bony tenderness over fracture site, deformity, swelling, limited range of motion, positive compression test. KEY NEGATIVES: No open wound (rules out open fracture), no crepitus unless severe.

includes.patient_friendly: all at once or very quickly

red_flags: Open wound with bone visible - open fracture, call 911
Severe deformity with neurovascular compromise - cold, pale, pulseless hand, call 911
Severe pain with numbness/tingling - possible compartment syndrome or nerve injury
Elderly patients with minimal trauma - possible pathological fracture, needs urgent evaluation
High-energy trauma - possible associated injuries, needs urgent evaluation
